title: Why Is This 65 km Strip So Important?

beats.text: This strip of land is only about sixty-five kilometres wide. Yet it links three countries to the rest of their alliance.
Close it, and Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania lose their only direct land link to Poland.
On the map it is called the Suwalki Gap. It lies between Belarus and the Russian region of Kaliningrad.
It is about three things. The distance, the terrain, and the lack of any alternative.
Many assume that a strip like this must be a fortress. In fact, it is mostly farmland, forest and small roads.
First, the distance. From Warsaw to Vilnius is around four hundred kilometres, and almost all of it crosses this narrow corridor.
Second, the terrain. Lakes and forests slow movement, and only a few paved roads cross it.
Third, there is no alternative route by land. The Baltic Sea is the only other way.
Now the other side. Planners say the risk is smaller than it looks, because both sides have far more to lose.

beats.text: One last distinction. A narrow gap is not a closed door. It is a place that is watched very closely.
